en.title: Dower or Mehr: What Are Your Rights?
en.directAnswer: Dower, also called mehr or moharana, is money or property promised to the wife as part of a Muslim marriage. The kabinnama is an important document. Whether an amount is due now, later or after divorce depends on the recorded terms and applicable law.

atAGlance.whoFor: A spouse wants to understand dower written in a Muslim marriage.
atAGlance.mainRule: Dower, also called mehr or moharana, is money or property promised to the wife as part of a Muslim marriage. The kabinna
atAGlance.updateStatus: Do not state a universal prompt/deferred rule without checking the kabinnama and applicable law.

en.lawMeaning:
A divorce or dissolution does not automatically erase a lawful dower claim.

This page gives a general route. A person’s exact rights can change because of facts, documents, deadlines, legal status, court orders or later amendments.
steps: Read the exact dower amount and terms.
If unpaid, identify the correct legal claim route.
Do not sign a waiver you do not understand.
evidence: Relevant official notices, receipts, and correspondence
en.simpleExample: A kabinnama states a dower amount, and the husband says it was paid in cash years ago. Both sides should look for receipts, witnesses and other reliable evidence.
commonMistakes: signing away a claim without advice.
en.specialistTrigger: Disputed payment; waiver; settlement; death; large amount; foreign marriage documents.
